milestone.title: lifecycle=complete ceremony — auto-promote on reviews pass + W-LC-TERMINAL validate warning

intent.outcome: mp reviews pass --verdict ok auto-promotes lifecycle=done → complete when the legacy-shape triple is present; mp validate surfaces W-LC-TERMINAL for stuck non-terminal lifecycles that look finished. Agents and humans stop leaking the done/complete gap.

problem.description: M143 and M144 shipped with `lifecycle=done + spec_status=verified + execution_status=done`. Only `complete` is in `LIFECYCLE_TERMINAL` (crates/mp-model/src/milestone.rs:58) — `done` is non-terminal. The triple reflects the executor's 'I'm done' write but skipped the ceremonial `mp milestone complete` write. Two reinforcing factors: (a) `mp reviews finding resolve` only auto-exits `remediation → done`/`self-reviewed`; on a non-remediation milestone it no-ops on lifecycle promotion (crates/mp/src/reviews.rs:875-902). (b) `mp reviews pass` validates only `execution_status == done` (crates/mp/src/reviews.rs:287-290), so a `lifecycle=done + execution_status=done + spec_status=verified` milestone can pass review without ever being promoted to the canonical terminal. `mp validate` doesn't gate the inconsistency either. Result: human readers of `raul status` and downstream tooling that keys on `LIFECYCLE_TERMINAL` see different things depending on who shipped the milestone and which ceremony was followed. The fix is symmetrical — close the ceremony gap with one auto-promote hook + one machine-checkable warning, mirroring how resolve_finding already auto-exits remediation when its precondition is met.

acceptance_criteria.description: `mp reviews pass --verdict ok --reviewer <who>` on a milestone with `lifecycle=done` + `spec_status=verified` + `execution_status=done` auto-promotes the lifecycle to `complete` and sets `lifecycle_at = Some(now_rfc3339())` only when the existing value is missing. Idempotent: re-running on a lifecycle=complete milestone leaves lifecycle=complete and lifecycle_at unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.description: `mp reviews pass --verdict changes-needed` does NOT promote the lifecycle. The verdict 'changes-needed' is a remediation signal; the milestone stays at its current lifecycle (typically `done` or `self-reviewed`) so the next finding add / resolve cycle exits to the correct pre-remediation state.

findings.description: F-02: Validate/promote asymmetry. W-LC-TERMINAL in crates/mp/src/validate/plan.rs:562-583 fires for ANY non-complete/non-cancelled lifecycle when exec=done + spec=verified (e.g. lifecycle=self-reviewed after a partial write or migration). But the auto-promote in reviews.rs:310 only fires for lifecycle=done. Result: validate tells the user to run `mp reviews pass --verdict ok` to fix a stuck milestone, but for lc=self-reviewed the pass succeeds without promoting. The warning's advice is unactionable for non-done lifecycles. Fix: narrow W-LC-TERMINAL to lc==done (matching auto-promote scope) OR generalize the auto-promote. Narrowing is safer — does not risk disrupting the active review loop.

findings.description: F-01: Auto-promote condition in record_review_pass has a redundant clause. crates/mp/src/reviews.rs:310 reads `lc != "complete" && lc == "done"` — the first clause is implied by the second. Either drop the redundancy or generalize (current form obscures intent). Trivial cleanup.
